overview.title: The Living Canvas Competition
overview.heading: Where Curiosity Meets Creativity
paragraphs: The Living Canvas Art & Life Sciences Competition invites scientists, researchers, students and artists to explore the beauty and complexity of life through visual expression.
We welcome original scientific photographs, microscopic images, research videos, digital illustrations, data visualizations and artworks inspired by the life sciences.
The competition celebrates both the scientific discoveries that reveal the extraordinary nature of living systems and the artistic interpretations that encourage us to see life differently.
Participants are invited to share their work, communicate the science behind their creations and contribute to an interdisciplinary community of discovery.
Selected submissions may be featured in The Living Canvas digital exhibition, with outstanding entries recognized through juried awards.
overview.motto: Discover Life. Express Science. Inspire Curiosity.

items.name: Division I — Science Through Research
items.text: For works originating directly from scientific research, observation, experimentation or scientific imaging.
items.includes: Includes microscopy, research photography, biological imaging, simulations, data visualization and research videography.

items.name: Division II — Science Through Art
items.text: For original creative works inspired by scientific concepts, biological structures or living systems.
items.includes: Includes illustration, photography, painting, digital art, animation, sculpture and mixed-media works.

items.name: Scientific Photography

items.name: Microscopic & Biomedical Imaging

items.name: Scientific Videography

items.name: Scientific Illustration

eligibility.title: Who Can Participate?
eligibility.intro: The Living Canvas Competition welcomes submissions from individuals of diverse academic, professional and artistic backgrounds, including:
notes: Individual and collaborative submissions are welcome.
Participants are not required to have formal scientific or artistic training. However, all submissions must demonstrate a meaningful connection to the life sciences.
Participants under the age of 18 must obtain permission from a parent or legal guardian.
All participants must have the necessary rights and permissions to submit and publicly exhibit their materials.

guidelines.title: Submission Guidelines
guidelines.intro: We welcome original works that explore scientific discovery, biological complexity or artistic interpretations of the living world.
requirements: An original photograph, video, illustration or other visual artwork.
A title for the submitted work.
A brief description of the artwork.
An explanation of its connection to the life sciences.
Information about the techniques, materials or scientific methods used.

technical.label: Images
technical.text: JPG, JPEG or PNG. High-resolution files are strongly encouraged, preferably at least 2,000 pixels on the longest side.

technical.label: Videos
technical.text: MP4 or MOV, preferably between 30 seconds and 5 minutes.

technical.label: Physical artworks
technical.text: Submit high-quality photographs of the original work.

technical.label: Data visualizations and illustrations
technical.text: Submit a high-resolution digital image or an accessible video format.

integrity: Scientific images must accurately represent their original subjects and underlying research. Any significant image manipulation, artificial colouring, compositing or computational processing should be disclosed.
Generative AI must not be used to fabricate scientific findings or misrepresent research data. Any use of generative AI in creative submissions must be disclosed.
Participants are responsible for obtaining all necessary permissions relating to research materials, collaborators, intellectual property and identifiable human subjects.
selection: Submissions will be reviewed for scientific relevance, artistic merit, originality and their ability to communicate meaningful ideas about the living world.
Selected works may be featured in The Living Canvas online exhibition and future educational or exhibition initiatives.

judging.title: Judging & Selection
paragraphs: Submissions will be evaluated through an interdisciplinary approach that considers both scientific significance and artistic expression.
Our aim is to recognize works that reveal meaningful aspects of the living world, demonstrate creativity and encourage audiences to engage with scientific ideas.
The judging process will consider scientific relevance, aesthetic quality, originality, communication and technical execution.
Criteria will reflect the distinct objectives of research-based and science-inspired artistic submissions.

awards.title: Celebrating Excellence
paragraphs: The Living Canvas Awards recognize outstanding contributions to the intersection of life sciences, visual arts and scientific communication.
Through these awards, we celebrate individuals whose work demonstrates curiosity, creativity, scientific understanding and the ability to inspire new perspectives on the living world.
Selected finalists and award recipients may be featured in The Living Canvas exhibition, digital catalogue and related educational initiatives.
